intro: Long ago, many Americans belonged to a lodge. A lodge was a club with its own ceremonies, symbols and handshakes. Members met in rooms above stores. Some met in tall halls downtown. They called each other brother or sister.

Lodges did real work. They paid sick members. They helped widows and children. Some sold life insurance. In Boston, a Black Mason named Prince Hall spoke up. He used his lodge and his pen to fight slavery and ask for schools. People left out of some lodges built their own.

In this unit, you will meet Prince Hall and the men of African Lodge. You will learn how the Odd Fellows, the Eastern Star and the Knights of Columbus helped families. You will read real sources and compare groups. You will explain what people got from belonging.
bigQuestion: What did Americans gain by joining lodges and orders, and who had to build their own?

timeline.t: Prince Hall and 14 other free Black men become Masons in Boston (one historian argues 1778).
Prince Hall and others petition Massachusetts lawmakers to end slavery.
The Grand Lodge of England signs a charter for African Lodge No. 459.
The charter reaches Boston. Prince Hall also petitions for schools for Black children.
Thomas Wildey and four others start the first Odd Fellows lodge in America, in Baltimore.
Rob Morris writes the ceremony that starts the Order of the Eastern Star.
North Star Lodge No. 12, a Prince Hall lodge, is set up in Chicago.
Connecticut charters the Knights of Columbus, begun by Father Michael McGivney.
Joseph Cullen Root starts the Woodmen of the World in Omaha.
Chicago's Masonic Temple skyscraper is finished at State and Randolph.
The Shriners finish Medinah Temple in Chicago.
Connecticut's grand lodge becomes the first mainstream one to recognize Prince Hall Masonry.

words.d: a local group of members of an order, or the room where they meet
a large club or society with many local lodges that share the same rules
a ceremony that makes a person a new member of a group
an official paper that gives a group the right to meet and act
a written request, often signed by many people, asking leaders to do something
the group of elected people who make a state's laws
to accept another group as real and equal members
a place that keeps old papers and records safe so people can study them
when members of a group help each other, often by sharing money in hard times
small regular payments that members give to their club
a plan where people pay a little money now to get help if something bad happens later
argued about, because people disagree about whether it is true

test.q: Who founded African Lodge in Boston?
test.why: Prince Hall led the free Black Masons who formed African Lodge in Boston.

test.q: What did African Lodge receive from the Grand Lodge of England?
test.why: The Grand Lodge of England signed a charter for African Lodge No. 459 in 1784.

test.q: What did Prince Hall's 1777 petition ask the Massachusetts legislature to do?
test.why: The 1777 petition asked lawmakers to end slavery, using the idea of a natural right to freedom.

test.q: What happened after lawmakers turned down the 1787 school petition?
choices: The community opened an African School in 1798
test.why: In 1798, an African School opened in the home of Primus Hall, Prince Hall's son.

test.q: Why do careful writers say "1775, though one historian argues 1778"?
choices: Oscar Alleyne's 2026 paper argues for a later date
Nobody knows who Prince Hall was
The charter was lost at sea
test.why: Oscar Alleyne's 2026 paper argues the men were made Masons in 1778, so the date is now debated.

test.q: Where can students study Prince Hall lodge papers from 1902 to 2006?
choices: The Woodson Regional Library in Chicago
test.why: The Prince Hall Freemasonry Archives are in the Harsh Collection at the Woodson Regional Library.

test.q: Which word means members help each other, often with money in hard times?
test.why: Mutual aid means members help each other, as lodges did with sick pay and burial money.

test.q: About how many adult men belonged to a lodge around 1910, by David Beito's estimate?
test.why: Beito estimates about one in three adult men belonged to a lodge around 1910.

test.q: Which order uses three chain links for Friendship, Love and Truth?
test.why: The three links are the symbol of the Odd Fellows.

test.q: How is the Eastern Star different from most other orders in this unit?
choices: It was started by a priest
Women and men join it together
test.why: The Eastern Star is an order that women and Masons join together.

test.q: Why did Father McGivney start the Knights of Columbus?
choices: To help Catholic men protect their families
To write a petition about schools
test.why: McGivney wanted Catholic men to have their own order to protect families and share their faith.

test.q: What was special about some Woodmen of the World gravestones?
choices: They were carved to look like tree stumps
test.why: The Woodmen once gave members markers carved like tree stumps.

test.q: The claim that Chicago's Masonic Temple was the tallest building in the world is best called what?
test.why: The claim is disputed because a New York building was taller if you count its tower.

choices: The Knights of Columbus were chartered
A mainstream grand lodge first recognized Prince Hall Masonry
test.why: In 1989, the Grand Lodge of Connecticut became the first mainstream grand lodge to recognize Prince Hall Masonry.

test.q: What do African Lodge and the Knights of Columbus have in common?
choices: Both were started by people left out of other groups
Both were started by Rob Morris
Both were part of the British army
test.why: Black Masons in Boston and Catholic men in New Haven both built their own orders when other groups did not include them.

write.prompt: Why did people build their own lodges and orders? Choose two groups from this unit, such as African Lodge and the Knights of Columbus. Use at least two facts or sources from the unit to explain what each group gave its members.
tips: Name each group and the person who started it.
Use one date and one source, such as a petition or Beito's estimate.
Use unit words like charter, mutual aid or petition.
Say what members got and who had been left out.
End with one sentence that answers the question.
